title: A velocity-field halting detector in forced viscous flow
exact_target: At fixed positive computable viscosity, can every machine and input be effectively realized by a unique zero-pressure global smooth forced Navier–Stokes flow on $T^3$, whose force has horizontal support in a time-independent compact subset of $(0,1)^2$ and finite-interval derivative bounds, such that some velocity component $u_3$ exceeds 1/2 in the fixed strip $1/32<y<1/8$ at some time exactly if the machine halts?
